utterances.text: Not right. The situation was quite tense. We -- I had to request the American major to use whatever means possible in order to fulfil the request I was making. I indicated that whatever happened, I would not leave that place without this equipment, and I think that at one point the major said that indeed, he would use any means so that I can fulfil my demand, and I think I said to the major that probably took them -- the colonel, sorry that, he probably didn't wish to have tanks rolling through his barracks, so indeed we ended up getting the equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is it your testimony today that Mr. Blagojevic was the commander over there at that particular location at that particular time?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, though he was dressed in civilian clothes, he was obviously the commander of that -- of that place, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's based on your investigation since then, or is that based on who you perceive to be the highest-ranking officer in the field at that headquarters at that particular time? Which one is it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: My personal experience is the one of June 1996, but Mr. Richard Butler, who did the military analysis of all the documentation we retrieved from the Bratunac Brigade, will probably give you the details that enable him to say that Colonel Blagojevic was indeed the commander of the Bratunac Brigade during that period of time of July 1995 that we are considering here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, see, there you go. That wasn't my question, now, was it? My question was back in 1996. There is no doubt -- there is no doubt, and you don't have to volunteer any information, that back in 1995 in July Mr. Blagojevic was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade. We can agree on that.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we're talking about 1996. MS. DE LA TORRE: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. De la Torre. MS. DE LA TORRE: I would object. While Mr. Ruez is perfectly capable of defending himself, the argumentative nature of these questions, as well as the fact that he's not allowing the witness to answer the question, is objectionable and unprofessional.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May I be heard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's hear the witness. We can judge. Let's hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That follows 1995. Okay? So we're at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters. I asked you a specific question. Please answer my question. Is it your testimony today that at that particular time Mr. Blagojevic was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, or is it your belief, based on the fact that he was the highest-ranking officer at that location at that particular moment? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What made me believe in June 1996 that Colonel Blagojevic was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade that day in June 1996 is because he was the person to which Major Golic was talking to when he was requesting clearances to do or not to do things, that Lieutenant Lazar Ostojic was addressing the colonel as his boss, that the American major with who I was, Major Zeijak [phoen] seemed to consider Colonel Blagojevic as the head of this brigade that day, June 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, a major is above or below a colonel?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time of the events, Colonel Blagojevic was Major Blagojevic indeed.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1996 he was colonel. In 1995, he was major, if I'm not wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm talking about 1996. That's where we are. We haven't gone to 1995.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So as far as I remember, Colonel Blagojevic in his rank was colonel in 1996, in June 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he outranked the major.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VRS -- the VRS Major Golic, yes, as well as the Lieutenant Lazar Ostojic, yes, but -- yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, and you said that it was tense, but all of you sat down and had a rakija with Mr. -- with Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a kind of compulsory tradition when you enter contact with some VRS officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Compulsory? What, they threaten you that you can't leave the area unless you sit down and drink rakija?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But it's hard to build any kind of even fake but immediate good relationship if you refuse having a drink in such circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a drink under those circumstances was offered in good faith, was it not?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's assume a drink is always offered in good faith, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicated that you had the major from the US army. He was what, SFOR at the time?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: IFOR at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: IFOR. Okay. Was he by himself or did he have troops with him?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had troops with him outside of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was there to protect you -- to offer you security.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All of our movements in the area were under the security coverage of multinational division north and of the American forces were based in Camp Lisa, Republika Srpska, just north of Vlasenica town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many soldiers did he have with him?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Though, we were always part of the operational plan in order to show us what was happening around us. I don't know, a company of "Bradley" and some of our troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicated that you had made a request, they didn't comply with your request, so that's when you went to IFOR. And I take it it was the Americans, as opposed to some other unit. And they were there to assist you. So you had arranged this trip, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had an appointment with Major Golic, in front of the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade that day, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. While you were at the brigade headquarters, did you ask the -- the major if he could provide some assistance in seizing documents for you, carrying them, since your -- how was it? Your backpack wasn't big enough to carry all these documents?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask him, since the goal of this mission was to find mass grave sites and not a search mission, and it was pointless for me to ask him anything in that sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought the goal of the mission at that point was to seize those helmets.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the goal of that last hour of that mission that lasted some ten days, but every day we were hitting mass grave sites.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask the major perhaps to secure the headquarters to make sure that now that you had been there that at least the -- the headquarters would be secure from the destruction of any -- of any documents? Did you ask for any help?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We already at that time had made the assumption that the clean-up process in these headquarters was already done, since this possibility was already there as soon as the photographs of Nova Kasaba had been showed publicly in front of a UN General Assembly in August 1995. So at that point, no, there was no -- no immediate urgency to try to prevent further more disappearance of documents. And anyhow, I confirmed that I was not in a position at that time to create a mission that had been designed to focus on capturing documentation, since we still at that time did not know what the crime bases we were talking about was a real one or was just other assessments and rumours and hearsay, like you already said several times before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So by that point you had made some assumptions.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like everyone does, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And might it be correct that even before that time you had made some assumptions?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I arrived there with a total blank mind and open mind in July 1995, if this is what you want me to -- to say or not say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm not trying -- I didn't say 1995, but at some point early on in the investigation you formed some assumptions; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You form 200 assumptions a day when you are conducting an investigation, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. And one of the assumptions was there is no need, at least in 1996, to go to the headquarters because you assumed that the people there who were running the headquarters would have destroyed the documents because after all, if they're guilty, that's what guilty people would do; right? So that's an assumption.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not there that. Again, I repeat. Had I had the possibility at that time, in terms of manpower, organisation, or whatsoever, to conduct an investigation in that place, that would have been done. It's one of the first things, indeed. You would think would have to be done one day. So the earliest is always the best. But it was not possible to do that in 1996. I repeat, if that would have been possible, I would have been very happy to do that in 1996 versus in 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree. Early is better than late. But nonetheless, the assumption had been formed early; isn't that what you indicated earlier?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our unit in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps at that time could have been considered as an interesting place to go and conduct searches, at least to have a quick idea as early as possible of who was who and in what capacity at the time of the events. But again --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I apologise. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But again, it is not a question that it was considered not important or too late, because it is also never too late. And you know that because even in 1998 we still could find things, but we just couldn't materially take such a course of action in 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And to refresh -- to refresh your memory, you never made those requests in writing. That was your testimony earlier; right? Because the assumption was we don't have the resources, let's do this other work. When the resources come or we have the opportunity to conduct those searches and seizures, then we'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, that's not the way the thing happened. Things had to happen in a certain chronology. Priority 1 was to interview witnesses and identify possible crime scenes that could then be analysed in order to corroborate their declarations. That is phase 1, 1995. Continued 1996 and even later. 1996 was a year devoted to identify these places described by the witnesses and mainly try to identify and locate all the primary mass grave sites. By the end of the year 1996, there was an article in Newsweek titling "Genocide without corpses," since all the primary graves had been disturbed in 1995, we only exhumed about 500 bodies by the end of 1996, though the main mass graves were exhumed that year. So 1997 was a year where we -- our main priority was to identify and locate the secondary mass grave sites. Only when all this was finalised and that we knew that potentially we had enough mass graves to match the unbelievable account made by the witnesses could we then seriously start to consider identifying the people who are responsible for these facts. But we had no absolute certainty on these facts before we started in fact exhuming secondary mass grave sites. We could not have a real assessment of how -- of what was really the scale of what we were working on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I'm correct, it wasn't until 1998 that you began to have some suspicions that the Bratunac Brigade might have been involved. Is that what you're saying? Is that what you want the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying that. You know very well that this suspicion is an obvious thing as early as 1995, due to the proximity of the Bratunac Brigade to all the crime scenes that we call the area "south." But I repeat again and again that taking action on this brigade was not the primary focus of this investigation, since when this investigation started we didn't even have one dead body, in terms of criminal facts we were working on. So first, we created -- I mean, we created -- we unravelled the facts. And once we had these facts, we were in a position then to develop the investigation on the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So in 1995, you had -- you formed a suspicion that the Bratunac Brigade was involved because of its location; is that correct? Yes or no? Back in 1995, based on your earlier lengthy answer.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I already have answered yes to this several times. Unlike 25.000 people who were deported and ended up in Tuzla, who also had in mind that what happened to them had any connection with the Bratunac Brigade, since it was the town just north to the enclave, indeed one could easily make the assumption during the summer 1995 that Bratunac Brigade had most probably something to do with what was happening. But it was a thought that everyone could have at that time in the area, even only if it was based on hearsay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And that's what I was trying to get you to admit. But that back in 1995, you began to form some assumptions that were perhaps logical, given the location of the Bratunac Brigade, that they must have been involved.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already answered this several times, and I agree to even accept your summary of it. No problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now -- now we can move on to the next section. Did you make contact with -- with Colonel Blagojevic after this -- this meeting that you had back in 1996? Did you attempt to meet with him again?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I -- I mean, not in 1996 anyhow.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we got in 1996 at one point during a mission information that Major Blagojevic was no more at the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was in Banja Luka, by the way, where you have a field office; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he was when I was told that he had left Bratunac, and we never had a field office in Banja Luka. We were just borrowing a room when we were conducting interview missions there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I stand corrected. But that room would be used often for interviews; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time we used it was end of 1999, and I think Major Jokic was the among the first to go to that place, but 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you were in this case until 2000, 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With the Court's indulgence for one second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the second time that you went to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was for the search operation that was conducted mid-1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the same place where it was in 1996?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly the same place, since in 1996 it was a container located in front of the building that is at the entrance of the Bratunac Brigade. And in 1998 the search was conducted in the part of a building at that time used as the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in -- okay. The -- let me rephrase the question. In 1996, was it located in the same place where it was located in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at the Bratunac Brigade in 1995. I cannot tell you exactly -- I mean, yes, the brigade was located at the same location, but the actual headquarters might not have been in the same place in 1995 as they were in 1996. But the brigade, yes, didn't move from the Kaolin factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Maybe -- maybe I'm not phrasing the question right, but -- and perhaps you can refresh my memory. I thought we saw some videos and some exhibits and some photos and there was a whole lot of narrative where often you would be leading the Prosecutor, rather than vice versa -- where you were describing the Bratunac town, various buildings in Bratunac, including the Bratunac Brigade headquarters. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I thought maybe I was incorrect. Now, I take it you identified those -- those markings on the photos; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to identify them, you'd have to be aware of what they are.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you want to be exact; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the footage and the photos would allow someone that if they actually went -- physically went to that location, they would be -- actually be able to identify photo, building; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the only way, but this is one of the ways, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you were able to identify what the building looked like or which building it was back in 1995 where the Bratunac Brigade headquarters were located. In 1996, you go to Bratunac to collect helmets and other gear, not to interview, not to collect documents, not to seize the compound, but to collect certain items. I take it that you knew exactly what compound, what building, what location you were going to before you got there; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. It was -- we had been, I think, in Bratunac town only once before we went to take this equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought you'd only been there -- the first time was in 1996.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in 1996 -- in April, we went to Bratunac town in order to identify the Old School, as well as the hangar. The second time we entered that town was indeed to collect the equipment in the container in front of the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So now we have you there twice in 1996 and twice failing to take any precautionary measures to locate any documents, because after all, you had made the assumption that documents would have been destroyed because after all, the assumption was back as early as 1995 that the Bratunac Brigade was involved because of their location, so there's no need to search for the documents that might prove who might have been involved.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You are again twisting completely what I have developed, I think, in length so far, which is that the reason why we did not focus on brigade searches in 1996 is that our first missions on the ground were designed to corroborate witnesses' testimonies and ensure that we were indeed facing a crime and not a lot of rumours. So in 1996 there was absolutely no intention to disregard that aspect. There was no preconceived opinion about the fact that it was useless. It was absolutely something that was urgent to be done. The only thing is that it was a material impossibility for me at that time to conduct such operations in 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But now we're talking about your second visit. You're there the second time. Did you know by your second visit to Bratunac, where you are accompanied by this American major and his troops, did you know by then where the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade were located; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know. I discovered that location that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have to ask directions from the folks in Bratunac, or was it the major that assisted you, or did you look at a map? How is it that you located it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before leaving Camp Lisa, we had what is called an operational briefing, where we were shown a map, the position of the forces that would secure our action, and on that map -- it was not even a map; it was an aerial photograph -- no, sorry, in 1996 it was just a map. We got a photo later. And we were shown where the location of the brigade is. Then we were put in vehicles. And when I stepped out of the HUMVEE, I was in front of the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade that I saw that day for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, let me get back to my question that I asked about 20 minutes ago. Was the headquarters that you visited back in 1996, based on the photograph that you were shown in your debriefing before you went off to the field, is that the same place where the Bratunac Brigade headquarters is located based on the photograph and footage and testimony that we've had on your direct examination; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that enables us to pinpoint the location of the Bratunac Brigade in July 1995 is based on the testimonies and the sketches provided to us by the Dutch witnesses who were in Bratunac town and who were going to the Bratunac Brigade facility, where they were having lunch. They drew sketches. They pinpointed the Kaolin Factory as being the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade. The little building in which we conducted the search in 1996, so the headquarters in 1996, this little building is pinpointed by these witnesses as being the -- the facility where the military police was back in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right up front.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right up front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before -- where the gate is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the gate is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so for the members of -- of the Trial Chamber, as you drive up to the -- that area, there's a fence with a little side building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that side building, it would be sort of where -- where the security would be for the compound.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what is pinpointed by the UN soldiers who went to this facility during the days of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And there is a -- right by the fence over there, there's a lengthy building, and that's where the military police would be located.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to these witnesses, yes, that was the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then you would have to drive a little bit or walk, you know, 20 or 30 metres at best, maybe 20 metres, and there would be a building, and that's where the factory is located.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's a fairly large compound; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there are many different entrances.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, and my memory may serve me wrong, but at least three entrances in that building.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, I don't know. Our search was limited to what we were told was the headquarters of the brigade. We did not search nor visit the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the two hours you were there, did you make any inquiries where the brigade was headquartered back in 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean when I was -- when I was there in June 1996?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah, having a rakija, sitting -- you know, you're an investigator, everybody is calm and relaxed, having a cigarette, having a little bit of coffee. Did you say, "By the way, where were you guys situated?"

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When -- let me finish. No, this is not the way we acted at that time. Since I had asked two questions -- two precise questions to Major Blagojevic that he consciously refused to answer, it was clear that it was pointless for me in such circumstances to try to get any kind of additional information from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever eventually find out where the brigade headquarters were located back in July 1995? And that's a yes or no. You don't have to go into a lengthy explanation.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, maybe -- I want to make sure I'm correct. So in 1996, you go to where you assume are the headquarters of the brigade. You don't know where they were in 1995. But until -- from 1995, when you began as the chief investigator in this case, until you quit back in 2001, you never made any inquiries as to where the Bratunac Brigade headquarters were back in July 20th -- back in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot let you present the things like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Well, correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to correct you. The inquiries were made. It's just that the answer did not come. I have no recollection that Momir Nikolic did answer any question -- any -- provide any information on this. And no, we didn't get any information on this, aside, as I repeat, the information provided by the UN soldiers who were in Bratunac town and who were going to the Bratunac Brigade and who all say that this was the location of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me take it -- take it slowly here. First, can we agree on one thing, that as you sit here today as the witness, the summary witness for this entire case that you worked on from 1995 into 2001, plus the information that you have learned thereafter as a result of the Krstic case and what -- and other things that you might have learned since then, is it fair to say today that you do not know where the Bratunac Brigade headquarters were indeed, to borrow one of your phrases, indeed, back in July 1995? You don't know that today, do you? Specifically, what part of the building. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just recalled one thing at the moment. You are talking about it, and you will certainly have an opportunity to have that confirmed or not. But I think -- I recall that during the interview we had with Captain Momir Nikolic, he told us several times that he went back systematically to these headquarters, where he was spending most of his time sleeping and doing nothing, and that these headquarters where he had his bed were indeed -- was indeed this building at the Bratunac Brigade. But this can be checked in the records of his statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. You begin -- it sounds as if - and I have to say this with all due respect - it sounds as if you're blaming now, you're shifting the blame on Nikolic, Momir Nikolic, for not knowing where exactly the headquarters were for this entire brigade back in July 1995. Because after all, this is a fairly large complex. We have a building up front, and there's a huge factory. So is it not a fact today, sir, that you do not know exactly where in that compound the Bratunac Brigade headquarter was? You have an idea of the vicinity, someplace in this complex, but back on July 1995 or June 1995 or August 1995 you do not know exactly where in that location was Mr. Blagojevic's office, for instance? Isn't that a fact? Take your time.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that the compilation of the information that I have in my possession, it leads me to believe that the headquarters and the unit of the Bratunac Brigade were in 1995 located in the compound of the Kaolin Factory in Bratunac. I have no clue where the offices of the various components of the HQ were at that time. But as far as I know, the only thing I can say is that it was located at the Kaolin Factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That's the answer that I wanted to get, that you don't know exactly where it was located.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a precise location, the Kaolin Factory. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We can agree on that. There's no disagreement there.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay? Are you happy? Okay. But that's a big compound, is it not?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a fairly large compound in a small town, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I were to ask you today, based on the answer that I just received, if I were to ask you at this moment to draw us a layout of how the headquarters were at the time back in June and July and August 1995 of the Bratunac Brigade, you would not be able to tell us that, to draw us that layout; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just what I told you in detail just before. Indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So the answer is you do not know the layout of the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. I could not be able to pinpoint any precise office within this compound. I confirm that, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So there's no need for me to ask questions such as where Mr. Blagojevic's office was, Mr. Momir Nikolic was located where other departments where. There's no need for know go on, because the answer to all of those questions are that you do not know now, today, after all those years in the field investigating this particular case?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right. I would be unable to pinpoint his office after all these years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you mentioned Nikolic, and it kind of piqued my interest a little bit. I have to say this. You interviewed him, did you not?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I take it you invited him for coffee to Banja Luka before you had an interview with him. Right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To return on this coffee thing that you seem to appreciate so much, the reason why I said that we always start by this politeness piece with these officers is that we had been accused by a kind of open letter of the Minister of Defence of Republika Srpska, claiming that we were exhausting people during a 12-hour interview process, not providing them with water, not giving them food, constantly resorting to threat of arrest against them, violating their spiritual integrity and their national dignity and things like this. So just to tell you that indeed Captain Nikolic was treated like all other officers we summoned to come to Banja Luka and that most probably we gave him an opportunity to first go to the bar of this building, where he could have breakfast or whatever he wanted to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So the answer is yes, you gave him some coffee before the interview.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if we gave him. I don't know if he bought it at the bar. But he had a chance to sustain himself and relax before we were starting the conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that was in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, I believe the exact date is 15 December 1999, just in case you don't recall. Would that be more or less?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not have remembered the specific date, but yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. By that point, do you suspect that Momir Nikolic might have been involved in some of these incidents?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was suspected is that he certainly had a lot of knowledge about the events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you saying that up until that point you did not suspect him to be involved?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had absolutely no hard evidence about his direct involvement in the criminal events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "direct evidence," what are you talking about? A photograph of him actually committing atrocities?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an example or even witnesses telling that they saw him committing anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's why back as late as 15 December 1999, you invited him there as a witness rather than as a suspect.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the reason, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on to my next segment. And I think that we might almost be through. I want to talk a little bit about the 28th Division. Okay, you've heard of them; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicated on direct examination that in -- that you believe that there were about 5.000 soldiers of the 28th -- roughly, give or take a few. But that was basically your estimation or the estimation, at least, I believe you put it, the internationals; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the estimation that -- that you -- that that was made was based on the number of weapons that they had; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, and as far as we know - but this investigation is, as you know, not on the 28th Division, but not also on the situation inside the enclave prior to its fall - but, and I'm sure that the Serb officers who are in this room will agree with this, that the number of soldiers was determined by the number of weapons, since every man indeed of fighting age had the potential to become a combatant in that context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And so am I clear to understand that your investigation -- you were disinterested at all in learning anything about the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's not that we were disinterested in learning anything about the 28th Division. It is that one cannot cope with everything. This investigation is an investigation on the crimes committed after the fall of the Srebrenica enclave. It's not an investigation designed to investigate crimes that might have been committed by the 28th. But in the course of this investigation, if we came across elements that could be useful for other cases, we did collect them. So it's not a question of not being interested. It's just a question of not -- it was not the subject of this investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you would agree with me that at the time of the fall of Srebrenica or before the fall of Srebrenica, in this area that was supposed to be demilitarised by the UN, inside that area, in that enclave, you had a fairly large cache of weapons and a significant number of combatants; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we eliminate the -- from your sentence the fairly large cache, information that I have no information upon, yes, indeed, there were a significant number of combatants in the enclave, and I don't think anyone disputes the fact that unfortunately this area has never been demilitarised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you would agree with me 5.000 weapons in a demilitarised area, that would put the numbers large for weapons?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, yes, I agree with you. And this is not disputed even by the Bosniak side, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you had indicated that -- that the 28th Division or members of the 28th Division were also committing some atrocities in Serb villages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you have no knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the rumours and the hearsay. I didn't work on that investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as you -- as far as you know, after all these years, you have no knowledge of Naser Oric going into Serb villages, killing Serbs, burning down their houses, committing atrocities himself in 1993, 1994, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know all the details of the accusations that the Serbs in this area and elsewhere make against the forces of Naser Oric. But again, I can only repeat that on that topic I have the same information available than any citizen, and I have not worked on this case, but I know -- I know the -- not only the charges brought by the ICTY against him but all the claims that both the population and the arrest officers have against him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So -- well, when did you hear of Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as summer 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he has quite a large reputation, does he not?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever try to interview him?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never tried to interview him formally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So does that mean informally you tried to interview him?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means indeed that I had a contact with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, that's good. So I take it during that contact you had a conversation, no?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how long did the conversation last?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably more than one hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I take it it wasn't about Naser Oric's handiwork that you were discussing at that time, and by that handiwork I mean what he was doing to the Serbs in and around the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two ways to collect information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why don't you answer my question first, and then you can talk about two ways of information collection.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I repeat -- again I, repeat, you are right when you say that that his actions were not the point of this contact, since again I repeat, the investigation I'm in charge of is not on that. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. But -- all right. Well, might I ask, because you kind of piqued my interest here. I've got to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you already knew about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, I did not. But now I'm very fascinated, to be honest with you. If you could tell me, about what year are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to be as precise as possible. December 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: December 1999. I take it that's -- that was in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's -- was he still a businessman, you know, black marketeering at the time when you met him?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I honestly don't know what his activities were in the area at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I know that the rumour says what you say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, could you show us the relevance of this set of questions. You have to understand that tu quoque is not a proper defence in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I totally agree with you, Your Honour. I totally agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We just want to know where you are going to lead us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would be more than happy to, Your Honour. The evidence will -- I think will come in through witnesses from the Prosecution and through our witnesses that the members of the VRS, while you had trained officers at the very top levels, that most of the soldiers were citizen soldiers that were from the surrounding area. So for instance, in Zvornik there would be citizens of Zvornik; in Bratunac, they would be from Bratunac. They were reservists. And they would spend two weeks on, two weeks off. Usually that was the -- the time period that they served. Where I'm getting at is this, Your Honour: That Naser Oric, it is clear -- there's out there, there's plenty of documentation, was going around, while Srebrenica was supposed to be demilitarised, he was sneaking out and he was killing Serbs and he was burning down their villages and he was committing atrocities. Now, here we are today in this trial. If you have an army that part of it -- part of that army -- part of that army is composed of reservists that live in that area that have family members that were lost during these atrocities, they on their own, whether they're serving or not serving, on their own may be committing crimes that are not known to the commander or where the commander is totally unaware of what's going on. If somebody is off duty for his two weeks and hears what's going on and has the opportunity to take personal revenge - I'm not justifying it. I'm not saying that this is a defence. But what I am saying: It is a logical consequence. And if somebody on his own, unknown to the commander, commits a crime, under the laws that we are dealing with here, surely command responsibility would not attach unless it fits within the strict criteria of the law. And that's all I'm trying to get at this point, Your Honour, that they did an investigation, it was selective in a way because they -- if you look and see who was participating during those interviews. You had a Prosecutor, Peter McCloskey, or Mr. Harmon there. You had Richard Butler, who was a military analyst. You had Frasier [phoen], another analyst. You had the professional investigator. All of them -- as we see here, the investigator comes in and anticipates what my cross-examination is going to be. And today he's even anticipating what the re-direct is. Surely they should have anticipated that hey, some of these atrocities might have been committed by individuals acting on their own, taking revenge for whatever reason. And I think that as a good investigation they have a duty not just to make an assumption, form a conclusion, and then try to reach for that evidence, excluding any other possibilities and excluding any other efforts to see maybe there's some exculpatory evidence here, maybe there are other avenues that are available. That's all I'm trying to say, Your Honour. And I'm trying to lay the foundation through this particular witness. But I totally agree with you that you cannot justify saying that an atrocity happened; therefore, you can commit another atrocity. That is totally unacceptable. Even one death is unacceptable. And I would not be here making that argument, and I pray that it never -- I never even insinuate that that is part of our defence, because it is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid that you could not get so much from this witness on this point. I think most of your argument will be presented during your case, that is, the Defence case, at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree with you, Your Honour. But I'm trying to also, since the gentleman is here. He might be able to help us out. He mentioned Naser Oric, that he had a meeting with him. I would like at least a few questions. And if you feel that I'm straying away too much, I'll be -- I'll be more than happy to back off. But if I could have some indulgence, Your Honour, just a few moments to see if I can get a few tidbits of information from the gentleman while he's still here before he leaves off for France because I don't have access to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may try your luck by asking a few questions, but not prolong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So now, when you met with Mr. Oric, did -- what was the topic? What was the nature of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The aim was not to collect any statement of -- out of him, since I insist this was not the topic of the investigation, but I was trying to obtain two informations from him: One was in connection with very -- I mean, one very specific event that was -- that happened, I'd say, at the beginning of the confrontation in that area, and that is information about the murder of -- the killing of a man named Zoran Zekic. It is -- Zoran Zekic was an SDS official in that area. And when the Muslim resistance started in that zone - I use their words - the -- the death of Zoran Zekic was used as a propaganda showing that Muslim forces could have victories in this place.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the microphone be adjusted for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- this man, for instance, was Zoran Zekic. We had other information about this event that we wanted just to -- we wanted to check what was the knowledge of -- of Naser Oric on this. And to put aside the investigation, in a way it's more connected with more -- with the situation of Miroslav Deronjic, all this. It's a bit a side -- a side investigation, if I can say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the other point was -- unfortunately, I don't have the name of the person in my head. It was in order to improve our knowledge about involvement of state security personnel during the operation in Potocari. So I wanted to use his personal recollection about one specific individual. It's not that I don't want to give you the name. I just don't recall it at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't need that. But did the strength of the 28th Division ever come up, given that there was battle activity in -- in the Zvornik area? I mean, you were aware of that; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, we are not, I think, here -- I mean, the Prosecution has never challenged the -- the fact that heavy battles were conducted in the forest. And when we talk about deaths, we only talk about prisoners who went through a detention process. We have never counted battle casualties as victims in this case. I mean, the Srebrenica case. But no, we didn't discuss any -- anything about this battle aspect during this interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is that because in your mind, as the investigator, along with the Prosecutors and the other analysts, in your mind that the -- the battle activities that happened in that Zvornik area between the 28th and the Zvornik Brigade were appropriate under the circumstances? Right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand exactly the question. But I mean, we have never, you know, challenged that point. I mean, we know that there was heavy fighting going on. We know that that was a heavy burden for all the officers who had to deal with it. And we know unfortunately that they couldn't properly fulfil their duties on this topic because of -- of the additional burden of having to conduct this security operation, like Colonel Popovic would call it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But -- but you don't dispute -- but just to make sure that I understand it, you don't dispute that there were -- there was heavy battle activity and that, at least from my understanding of your answer, that that battle activity was not necessarily improper under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, no, the battle activity is battle activity, and we have never charged, as far as I know, anyone for -- for the casualties that occurred during this combat activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are we going to be taking a break soon, Your Honour? If so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you've finished that subject and change --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I've finished that subject, Your Honour, and I don't want to take up the Trial Chamber's time. I'm trying to condense it so I can finish today. And I am -- I am confident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have the break now, and we will resume at twenty minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I'm going to switch to another topic. I want to focus your attention, if you could, to that one piece of footage that you introduced as a summary witness and which, I believe, it was Colonel, Colonel Karremans, is speaking with General Mladic the first time to time. Do you remember that footage?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And correct me if I'm wrong. It's my recollection, from watching the video, that at that particular meeting was initiated by Colonel Karremans. Is that -- is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember I made a mistake when I made a comment on this. I said that this first meeting had been done on the request of General Mladic. But indeed you're absolutely right. It was on the request of Colonel Karremans, as it appears clearly on the video footage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, during that meeting, it appeared to me that at least prior to the meeting Colonel Karremans had initiated -- had taken some initiatives of his own. And by that what I mean is that he had made some contacts, and in particular one of them being with the -- the BiH government in Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I honestly don't know if that is correct. I might indeed recall that -- that aspect. I don't remember if it was BiH government in Sarajevo. In my recollection it was the central command in Zagreb that he attempted to get in contact with, or maybe headquarters in Sarajevo, but probably certainly not the BiH government, I would think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So -- so as far as -- as far as your recollection goes - and it could be that I'm mistaken. I was under the impression from listening to that that, one, he had contacted either his folks in Zagreb, that is, the UN, but also he had some information from the government in Sarajevo, that information being that the folks in Potocari should be evacuated, you know, outside the area.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer on that point. His declarations are in the records. I would invite you to check them. I don't want to recall things --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- instead of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you have an opportunity to interview Colonel Karremans?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never interviewed Colonel Karremans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did somebody else interview him?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to read his -- his statement, the interview statement?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that was the case, it was probably in 1996. I don't have recollection of having read his statement in 1996, though certainly if he gave one I did, but I don't recall. I mainly recall his declarations that he made during the public hearing, the Rule 61 hearing, end of June, early July 1996 and it's content, but I don't recall having read a statement he gave prior to that situation, though he might have given one. I just don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do -- did you -- I recall receiving some disclosure material with respect to interviews or statements or forms that were filled out by Dutch -- DutchBat soldiers. Was somebody else covering that aspect of the investigation and you were focussing on -- on the mass graves and other areas?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a way, yes, since a team of Flemish speaking investigators was put together for the sake of that interview mission that first took place in Hassan, in a Dutch military barracks. I did not take part in that, aside on the point of preparing some questions for those who would go to this interview. This interview process, as far as I remember, was stalled a couple of times, because unfortunately at that time there were some financial problems at the OTP, so the process stalled for that reason at one point. And I was indeed on mission in Bosnia, in Republika Srpska, I think, during this interview process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Another -- another segment of some of the footage that we saw -- and as you might recall, I -- I stood up and I made an objection -- well, I was asking for a clarification. Well, maybe it was an objection as well, because as I recall, you had formed an opinion or a conclusion. And that was with respect to the blue helmets. Do you remember that section?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In the footage we see someone wearing a blue helmet that obviously belongs to the UN; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And obviously that person is not with the UN that's wearing it.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But in looking at that footage, based on the uniform that the -- the gentleman was wearing at the time, can you tell from whether he was a soldier or whether he was MUP?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to give you full satisfaction on this. When I said "on this footage you can see a Serb soldier wearing a blue helmet," I said on purpose -- I used on purpose a term that is quite large, "Serb soldier," since in the way I mean it, it is a word used for whoever is part of a unit resubordinated to the Drina Corps for the sake of the military operation. But you are right to pinpoint what you pinpointed. We know not from the uniform, but Mr. Butler will be the one providing you the details on this, that in this specific area we know for sure are present both soldiers who are professional policemen but embedded in companies formed by the CSB Zvornik in order to reinforce the army for specific military operations. So they are, in brackets part-time soldiers. They only go in combat for very specific situations. And on that same part of the road, that is, between Lolici and Kravica, with Sandici in the middle, are also present elements of a special police brigade, that is, a full-time combat unit. So indeed it could very well be that this soldier is either one or the other. So when I say "soldier," here it means a number of the VRS armed forces that day - because anyhow, he is in a combat operation where his unit is resubordinated to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I wasn't prepared to into this area, but I guess I need to clarify a little bit. You're not a military expert. We can agree on that, can we not?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Though I'm a reserve officer in the French army, indeed I am not a military expert.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Okay. And you're not here to testify as a military expert.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to leave that to Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly what I expect to happen, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. So -- and I am sure Mr. Butler is going to fascinate us with the issue of subordination, resubordination, and what have you. However, is it your understanding that everyone at all times during that particular -- during those particular days that were in that vicinity were subordinated or resubordinated, however you want to term it, to the army, or is that an assumption that you're making?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not an assumption. This has been one of the main topics during the trial of General Krstic. And as far as I understand the situation, this resubordination aspect is no more a topic, since the Trial Chamber has already ruled on this during the Krstic trial. But I am not an expert of that trial, where I was only a witness at one point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But -- okay. So it's based on that -- that trial that now you're saying that obviously he was a soldier, in your terms, that is, he was a member of the VRS because everybody there in uniform at that time, during those days, was subordinated to the VRS? It's an assumption that you're making.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not making this assumption. What I am saying is that as far as we know, both special police companies and special police brigade were two units resubordinated to the Drina Corps. But to assist you in where you probably want to lead me to is that I've never said that this soldier was a member of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't leading you there, but thank you for volunteering that information. I'm sure it's useful to the -- to the Trial Chamber. Now we can move on to the next area. How many hours would you estimate that you spent on this case or days or weeks or months, whichever is most convenient for you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Close to six years, including most of the weekends and most of the evenings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So for about six years, basically Srebrenica has been more or less your life.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And -- but you, of course, were not the only one investigating Srebrenica. There were others.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely, yes. A large team. If we pile up all those who participated at the moment or another, a very large team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's what I'm trying to get at, you know. I'm trying to figure out how large of a team was this.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would take you a long time to find out all these details, because the figures evoluted in the time. When I say a large team, counting everyone and counting in this all the exhumation team, all the people we were in contact with for whatever reason in this investigation, including the military personnel who assisted us, either by obligation or sometimes because they felt it was appropriate to do so. But if you are considering the investigation team, the maximum number of investigators that has ever been present at the same time in the team has never been above five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Would you consider this a -- a complex, highly complex case, medium complex? Where would the range be?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would leave it to others to assess the complexity of this case. I've been too close in contact with it to now give an assessment about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you saying you have no objectivity left as a result of the six years you spent on this case?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think my objectivity is absolutely intact. What I want to say is that if it is indeed a highly complex case, that I think we finalised quite well, I don't want to give me this compliment. I don't know if it was complex. We just did it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, it was neither meant as a compliment or any other way that you might have taken it. It was merely a piece of information that I was trying to get out of you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'll just tell you the reason why I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. And I won't push on it. Now, you left in -- in 2001, and it's my understanding - and I might be wrong - it was either before or right after or during the middle of the Krstic case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was close to the end of it, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Close to the end of the trial -- the Krstic trial?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that's been some time; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two years, a bit more than two years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two years. Right. Now, during that two-year period, someone who has spent six years of their life working on this -- working on a particular project, I would imagine you -- you followed -- you kept following the progress of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From a distance. But would it be fair to say that you -- you have spoken to your colleagues and friends?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because I came back twice to Europe and met my friends and colleagues and indeed got an update on the evolution of the situation compared with the time I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you say you came back to Europe. I take it it was outside of Europe.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And before coming here today -- well, before coming to testify, I should say, you did meet with the Prosecutors, did you not?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not since I am under oath, but I was here in the weeks before I was testifying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. How long were you here before you testified?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Three weeks.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would think. I arrived here Monday -- Sunday, 12th, starting Monday, 13th, to be precise. May, month of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the purpose for meeting with the Prosecution was to -- to assist them in putting together your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. Selecting the exhibits the Prosecutor intended to use for this trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And would it be fair to say that up until the time that you left, a few people, perhaps, you know, Mr. McCloskey being the exception, would have as much knowledge about the case as you would? Right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that's why it was necessary for you to assist their team - and it's a fairly large team, would you not say, that is working -- putting this presentation together? I mean, I see - one, two, three, four - four Prosecutors here in court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I came here to assist them. In fact, narrowing down the testimony compared to the one we did with during the trial of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And selecting the exhibits, since indeed I'm the only one from the team who was present when most of these pictures were taken, and among the ones who can for sure say what they represent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And during that time, as I understand it - and we got a copy of it the other night - the questions were more or less outlined for you, or the areas where there would be -- where you would be questioned on; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The chronology of -- of the testimony was outlined point by point, I'd say chapter after chapter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was that done by you or was that done by the Prosecutor that did the questioning?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was done by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you just look at and it say, "Okay, this is okay," or did you have some input into it, sometimes maybe informing her that she should add this or maybe relocate that chapter or ...?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Prosecutor, Stacy de la Torre, knows this case extremely well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask that question, now, did I?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know you didn't ask, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just answer my question.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But in order to answer properly your question, I have first to say that. If not, you would not understand my answer. Because of her knowledge, it was not a need for me to -- to change much regarding what she expected me -- what she expected from me during this testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So she wrote out that, and you looked at it, and you gave it your stamp of approval, as far as what you thought would be a good compilation of a summary of your investigation and of this case; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We agreed that indeed that was the minimum we could put together in order to -- to assist the Chamber to visualise the areas that the witnesses describe in the course of their various testimonies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said "we," meaning you and the Prosecution; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You as a witness, who no longer works for OTP, for the Office of the Prosecution, now in some kind of an expert capacity are working with them, assisting them to assist the Trial Chamber and the rest of us, hopefully, in the presentation of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're shaking your head. Does that mean yes?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We're trying to make a record here. That's all. All right. And that took about, what, two or three weeks you said?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those full days or half days? And weekends included.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was depended on the days. I didn't take records of our activities during these three weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah, but you've got almost a photographic memory. You can remember things from 1995. Surely you must remember whether -- how many hours, tell us, in general might you have spent with Ms. de la Torre and the other members of the team in assisting them in preparing your testimony? It's not a trick question, by the way.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it's not a trick question, but -- and we have to split the time spent in two -- in two different things. One is the time I spent with Stacy de la Torre, and part of it is time I spent myself in -- to review material. And as you know, for example, the videotape is three hours and a half, so you look at this entirely is three hours and a half. Then you have to re-look at it again because you realise that some -- I mean, some pieces, for example, would not be inserted at the right moments. I mean, I hardly can give you an estimate of time. I didn't pay attention to that, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, during that -- was it just you and Ms. de la Torre, or were -- did you speak with others?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, me and Ms. de la Torre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just the two of you. You didn't have a chance to speak at all with -- with Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not about the issue of this testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you speak about any other aspects of the case with either Ms. de la Torre or other members of the Prosecution team?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing specific, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "nothing specific," what does that mean? That's kind of a vague answer.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I have to keep it vague, because being under oath I don't want to say -- to say a straight no, we didn't talk about anything connected with the case. It's impossible for me not to speak about the case and the investigation when I am in contact with colleagues who worked with it. So for sure we probably discussed things, but no subject that I would be able to -- to recall now specifically, a very specific issue. Just in order to check if this would be something correct for you or not correct. So I just can provide this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But yes, we discussed the investigation. We discussed the case. I did it with every single person from the team who I meet, just about to make a little comment or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how many members all together on the team would you say you have spoken to? Because I'm trying to get a figure as well of how large this team is presently.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this time, though I don't think it's a secret, you have one -- an investigation team leader and two investigators who were -- sorry, three, two of them having been in the team since quite a while. The most ancient investigator in the team currently is Mr. Dean Manning, who will come and testify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then of course the four Prosecutors, plus their -- their assistants and --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I mean, I'm not focussing on the trial team. I only talk about the part I know about, which is the investigation team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you kept abreast of the negotiations that were ongoing at the time of your arrival between the Nikolic Defence team and the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't give any specifics about what was happening on that topic, but I knew that there was indeed a possibility that at least one of the defendants would plead guilty, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you were -- just -- you just learned of this information, but you didn't have -- for instance, nobody from the Prosecution said, "Hey, you know, we're negotiating, we're talking.
